articles.title: Khan Sir To Seek Anticipatory Bail Over Coaching Centre Vandalism Case In Patna
articles.rephrased_article: Khan Sir, a popular educator and YouTuber, will file an anticipatory bail petition in Patna civil court after being named in an FIR related to vandalism at his coaching center. The FIR alleges that a group of 15-20 people attacked the center, injuring two guards who fired shots in self-defense. Arvind Kumar Mahuar, Khan Sir's lawyer, claims the FIR is part of a conspiracy to defame him and that no actual charges have been filed against his client.

articles.title: Bihar BJP MLA Raju Kumar Singh Convicted For Woman's Death In 2018 Celebratory Firing
articles.rephrased_article: Raju Kumar Singh, a BJP MLA from Bihar, was convicted of culpable homicide for celebratory firing at a New Year party in 2018.  The court found him guilty under the Indian Penal Code and Arms Act for violating his arms licence conditions by firing a 0.22 bore pistol not allowed for such use. Singh's wife and two others were acquitted of related charges. The court noted that Singh, identified by multiple witnesses, fired the fatal bullet that killed Archana Gupta, a guest at the party.  The case is scheduled for sentencing on June 9th.
articles.civic_flag_reason: An elected official convicted for causing death due to reckless firearm use is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: New Ashok Nagar Debosmita Paul Couple Arrested From Bengal Over Delhi University Professor's Murder
articles.rephrased_article: Debosmita Paul, an assistant professor at Shivaji College, was found dead in her Delhi flat on Thursday.  Her sister, Devarati, discovered her body after repeated attempts to contact her proved unsuccessful. Police suspect foul play and are investigating the case as a murder.

articles.title: Celebratory firing death: Bihar BJP MLA convicted | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Nirbhay Thakur, a Senior Correspondent for The Indian Express, has been covering district courts in Delhi since 2023, focusing on high-profile cases.  He has written in-depth articles and investigations into several notable trials, including the acquittal of Surender Koli in the Nithari serial killings and an investigation into court acquittals in Delhi riots cases. Thakur is known for his procedural depth and ability to summarize complex legal documents for a general audience.
articles.civic_flag_reason: An MLA convicted for celebratory firing resulting in death, highlighting potential abuse of power.

articles.title: Ohio mass shooting: Multiple injured in Toledo Old West End festival, manhunt under way - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Multiple people were shot near a community street festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday afternoon. Toledo Police responded to reports of gunfire and discovered several victims suffering from gunshot wounds.  Mayor Wade Kapszukiewicz stated that eight people were injured but expected to survive. The incident occurred during the annual Old West End Festival, which features live music, food vendors, shopping, and home tours. Kevin Berry, a US Navy veteran with medical training, assisted injured individuals while police investigated the shooting.  The incident is being investigated by Toledo Police and authorities are urging the public to avoid the area.

articles.title: Odisha police arrest one person from Uttar Pradesh in connection with trafficking of minor girl - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha police have arrested Chandrapal Kushwah, 26, for marrying a minor tribal girl trafficked from Kankadahad area in Dhenkanal district to Jhansi.  The girl was lured with the promise of a job and subjected to sexual assault by multiple men over two years. The investigation will be expanded to uncover more individuals involved. Jitendra Mallick, Inspector-in-Charge of Kamakshyanagar police station, stated that the marriage is illegitimate due to the girl's age.

articles.title: Speeding SUV overturns after hitting bike and shop in Varanasi, 3 hurt | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A speeding black SUV crashed in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, injuring three people and damaging a roadside shop. Prince Sahani, 18 years and 6 months old, was driving the vehicle with his brother, Sahil Sahani, when it lost control after colliding with a motorcycle. The incident resulted in injuries to Ranganath Pandey, Vishwambhar Nath Chaurasia, and Meeta Sonkar, who were walking along the roadside.  The police have registered a case and are reviewing CCTV footage and eyewitness statements to determine the cause of the crash.

articles.title: Assault on women in Kochi: key accused held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ali Akbar, a native of Palakkad, was arrested by Kochi city police on Saturday from a hideout in Cherpulasery.  He is the prime suspect in an alleged assault on two young women that occurred around 4:30 a.m. on June 2nd at Chakkalapadam Road in Kaloor. With his arrest, four other suspects have been apprehended while six remain at large.

articles.title: Indian man shot dead in Philadelphia after delivering pizza to a housing complex after midnight - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anshul Kuncha, a 28-year-old Indian man, was fatally shot in North Philadelphia while delivering pizza boxes to a vacant unit at the Raymon Rosen Homes housing complex.  Police found three spent shell casings near the victim and his vehicle, which contained a pizza warmer still inside. Surveillance footage captured two individuals wearing dark clothing following Kuncha before the shooting occurred. Philadelphia Police Department Chief Inspector Scott Small confirmed that investigators are working on this lead and have identified the pizza shop where Kuncha worked, Pete's Pizza.

articles.title: Nine booked for illegal quarry blast in Anekal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anekal police have registered a case against nine individuals for allegedly conducting blasting operations without proper permits and safety measures at a stone quarry in Thammanayakanahalli village. The police received credible information about the activity, leading to an inspection where they found workers preparing for blasting using drilling equipment and explosive materials.  The police noted that no authorized blasting supervisor was present and explosives were stored unsafely, with quarry stones being loaded onto lorries for transportation.

articles.title: History-sheeter arrested for assaulting man, son - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Shyamkumar alias Thakaraparambu Kuttan, a history-sheeter, was arrested by Vanchiyoor police on Saturday for allegedly assaulting a man and his son. The incident occurred after the victim, Rajesh Kumar, honked at Shyamkumar who had blocked a road with his car.  The attack left the father with a fractured leg and his son with facial injuries. Police are seeking another suspect, Arun, who joined in the assault.

articles.title: Three arrested in Chebrolu double murder case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chebrolu police have arrested three individuals in connection with the murders of M. Venkata Lakshmi and her mother, G. Anthoboyila.  The suspects are Ponamala Sirisha, who harbored a grudge against the victims due to rumors about her character; Karri Prasad alias Basu, Sirisha's paramour; and Aasu Durga. The trio allegedly invited the victims to a birthday party in cashew orchards, where they were poisoned and later killed with boulders.  The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Delivery executive arrested for abetment of woman’s suicide in Gachibowli - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Gachibowli police have arrested a delivery executive, Sai Kumar Posti, in connection with the death of 23-year-old Molli Durga who died by suicide at an Elite Co-Living Hostel.  The woman's uncle, Devarampally Ravi Kumar, filed a complaint alleging that Posti had harassed and driven his niece to take her life after an argument over alcohol consumption. The accused is being held in custody pending further investigation.

articles.title: Kota priest hacked to death inside monastery, saints launch protest over delayed arrests | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A priest, Mahant Devanand Maharaj, was found critically injured and later died at a monastery in Kota, Rajasthan after being attacked by assailants. The attack occurred late Friday night while he was asleep, and police suspect an internal conflict within the Math committee as a possible motive.  Religious leaders are protesting the delayed arrests of those responsible for the murder. Ramdas Ji Maharaj, general secretary of the All India Sant Samiti (Hadoti Division), stated that they will not accept the body until the culprits are apprehended.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Murder of a religious leader with delayed arrests raises concerns about justice.

articles.title: MP teen battling for life after ‘stalker’ attacks her with axe, hangs her from rooftop | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Anand Mohan J, a Senior Correspondent for The Indian Express, has been covering Madhya Pradesh since 2017. He is known for his investigative work on topics including the decline of Naxalism, legal accountability, wildlife conservation (Project Cheetah), and public health issues.  His reporting has focused on the surrender of Maoist cadres in the state, as well as exposing institutional lapses within various sectors. Anand Mohan J's expertise has earned him recognition for his "Journalism of Courage" approach.

articles.title: NRI maths teacher from Australia, crores of propertyin India: Chilling murder plot by family members revealed - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Surbhi Sharma, daughter of an NRI maths teacher in Australia, learned that her father, Sunil Sharma, had been murdered after he mysteriously disappeared in India.  The Indian police arrested Satish Sharma, his wife, son, and a property dealer for plotting to kill the 66-year-old to gain control of his properties through a forged power of attorney. Sharma was lured to India with a property deal, given sleeping pills, and then killed by being struck on the head with a baseball bat. The police are still investigating whether Sharma's body has been found.

articles.title: Fake Doctors Found In Madhya Pradesh, Purchased Degrees For Rs 10 Lakh
articles.rephrased_article: In Madhya Pradesh, three doctors were arrested in Damoh for using fake MBBS degrees to secure government jobs. The investigation revealed that these doctors, identified as Dr Kumar Sachin Yadav, Dr Rajpal Gaur, and Dr Ajay Maurya, treated over 30-40 patients daily at Sanjeevani Clinics for two years.  The scam has raised concerns about the integrity of the public medical system in the state. Authorities are now conducting a verification drive across more than 2,000 contractual doctors appointed under the National Health Mission and Sanjeevani Clinics to ensure their credentials are legitimate.

articles.title: Chhattisgarh Man Travelling With Wife, Child Alleges Police Beat Him At Checkpoint
articles.rephrased_article: A young man traveling with his wife and child in Chhattisgarh was allegedly assaulted by the Arjuni police station in charge after he began recording a police interaction on his phone. The incident occurred during a late-night police checkpoint near Mujgahan-Potiadih bypass, where the man claimed to have been harassed despite traveling with his family. Police claim the rider refused to cooperate, became aggressive, and attempted to provoke officers by speaking loudly and recording videos.  The police station in charge, Chandrakant Sahu, allegedly assaulted the man after objecting to his behavior and video recording.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Police brutality against a citizen for recording an interaction is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: Driver held for illegal transport of river sand near Katpadi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J. Sugan, a 45-year-old driver from Dharmapuri district, was arrested by Katpadi police at the Christianpet police check post for illegally transporting river sand from Chittoor district in Andhra Pradesh to Tamil Nadu. The police seized the lorry and its load of river sand after finding it during routine patrol along the Tamil Nadu-Andhra Pradesh border.  A case has been registered, and an investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Accused in youth abduction case held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anish Nasar, also known as 'Attani Anish', a native of Mattancherry, has been arrested by Ernakulam Central police in connection with the alleged abduction and assault of a youth from Bengaluru.  The 43-year-old is listed in the police rowdy-sheeter register and was recently involved in an assault case at a tea shop in Kochi. He was released on bail after being remanded in judicial custody for that incident, but allegedly abducted the victim in a vehicle, assaulted him, and posted a video of the crime online.

articles.title: West Bengal Police recover large cache of arms hidden inside pond at Sandeshkhali - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: West Bengal Police's Special Task Force (STF) recovered a large cache of firearms and ammunition hidden in a pond belonging to Trinamool Congress functionaries Robin Das and Gopal Das in Sandeshkhali, North 24 Parganas district.  Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari praised the police for this major breakthrough, stating that it was part of efforts to restore law and order after years of illegal weapon use under the previous Trinamool regime. Rekha Patra, a BJP MLA who survived the Sandeshkhali violence in 2024, welcomed the recovery as a step towards normalcy.

articles.title: Boyfriend Kills Pregnant Woman, Police Find Her Skeleton
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old woman was found dead in a forest area near Lucknow after allegedly being murdered by her boyfriend, Vishal Pal, who is now hospitalized with a gunshot wound.  Pal, who had been arrested for the murder, allegedly confessed to the crime and fled from police custody while attempting to escape during an evidence recovery operation. The woman's body was discovered by local police and forensic teams, who collected evidence at the scene.

articles.title: UP Teenager Dies After Setting Herself On Fire, Lover In Critical Condition
articles.rephrased_article: A 19-year-old woman, Khushi, died and her alleged lover, Arun Kumar (21), remains critically injured after they set themselves on fire inside a locked room in Shikohabad, Uttar Pradesh. Amrish Kumar, the Shikohabad Circle Officer, said police received information about loud noises from the house and found both individuals with severe burn injuries.  Khushi succumbed to her injuries while undergoing treatment at SN Medical College in Agra. Police are investigating the incident, which appears to be linked to a love affair.

articles.title: From Rs 6,000 Salary To Rs 2 Crore In Assets: Odisha Engineer Under Scanner
articles.rephrased_article: Odisha Vigilance conducted simultaneous raids at nine locations linked to Assistant Executive Engineer Baikuntha Nath Behera, uncovering multiple luxury properties, high-value land holdings, and a significant amount of cash.  The searches, carried out across Bhubaneswar, Balasore, Jajpur, and Baliguda districts, are in response to allegations that Behera possessed assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. The operation is ongoing, with investigators examining the valuation of gold ornaments, bank deposits, investments, and other financial assets.  The total value of the assets allegedly accumulated by Behera is expected to become clearer once the searches and valuation process are completed.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article suggests potential corruption and abuse of power by a government official.

articles.title: Driver who allegedly dumped accident victim’s body on roadside arrested within 48 hours | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mehboob Lakeeb Mohammad Shaikh, a 40-year-old resident of Parner, was arrested by the Pimpri Chinchwad police for allegedly dumping the body of a pedestrian, Manojkumar Ramji Vishwakarma, after he was struck by a speeding vehicle on June 4th.  The incident occurred near Khalumbre on the Chakan–Talegaon road and the investigation revealed that Shaikh kept Vishwakarma's body in his vehicle before discarding it on the roadside in Shirur. The North Mhalunge police station filed an FIR under various sections of the BNS, including those related to rash driving and endangering human life, as well as the Motor Vehicles Act.

articles.title: Brother, Nephew Accused Of Killing NRI Over Property In Amritsar
articles.rephrased_article: Amritsar Rural Police have solved the murder of Australian NRI Sunil Sharma, revealing his brother Satish Sharma and accomplices conspired to usurp property worth Rs 5-6 crore.  The investigation, which began after a missing person report was filed on May 23rd, involved analyzing CCTV footage, phone data, and forensic evidence. The accused allegedly lured Sharma under the pretense of a property deal, sedated him, and struck him on the head before attempting to destroy evidence. Satish Sharma, his son Sunny Sharma, and property dealer Lakhwinder Singh have been arrested while two other suspects remain at large.

articles.title: ‘Should we throw flowers?’: Videos show Khan Sir reacting to firing incident amid police search | Patna News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Faizal Khan, also known as Khan Sir, a YouTuber and educator, is being sought by police after allegedly instructing his security guards to fire at a crowd outside his coaching institute.  Videos purportedly showing Khan commenting on the incident before students surfaced online, prompting police to appeal for calm and urge students not to be “misled”. Police are investigating the incident and have arrested two security guards employed by Khan’s institute over the firing. Khan’s lawyer has denied the allegations, claiming the FIR was lodged with a “retaliatory” intent.  Police are continuing efforts to trace Khan and have intensified security checks across the city.

articles.title: Strangled, Stuffed In Suitcase, Burnt: Punjab Man Kills Lover's Daughter
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old man, Gurwinder Singh, alias Gurpreet Gopa, from Punjab was arrested for allegedly murdering a 15-year-old girl whose body was found in a suitcase set on fire in a forest. The victim, the daughter of Usha Rani, had been missing since May 29th after being lured away under the pretense of marriage by Gurwinder who was in a relationship with her mother and frequently visited their home. Police are investigating further.

articles.title: Greater Noida Man Stabs Mother, Then Jumps Off Building And Dies
articles.rephrased_article: A 21-year-old man, Sagar Yadav, died after allegedly jumping from the fifth floor of a building in Greater Noida.  Yadav, who was reportedly mentally unstable, stabbed his mother during an altercation before taking his own life. He was declared dead at a nearby hospital where his mother is currently receiving treatment. Police are investigating the incident and have sent the body for postmortem.

articles.title: South Delhi hotel fire: Chef of B&B held as police say his ‘negligence’ may have contributed to blaze | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Keshav Negi, the chef of Flourish Stays bed and breakfast in South Delhi, has been arrested three days after a fire killed 22 people.  Police are investigating whether his alleged negligence contributed to the blaze, which broke out at the facility on Friday.  Negi is one of two individuals arrested in connection with the fire, alongside hotel owner Lavkesh Bajaj, who was booked under culpable homicide not amounting to murder. Police are also searching for Jay Mishra, the accountant, and Rakesh, the manager, as they continue their investigation into possible safety lapses that may have contributed to the tragedy.

articles.title: Police launch search for Guntur NRI family involved in job, visa fraud - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Jagarlamudi Madhukar and Anne Rama Nandana
articles.rephrased_article: Ibrahimpatnam police are investigating a visa and job fraud case involving an NRI couple, Jagarlamudi Madhukar and his wife, Anne Rama Nandana, who gained popularity on YouTube. The couple allegedly defrauded several job aspirants in Telangana by promising them jobs in the UK.  The police have registered cases in both Ibrahimpatnam and Hyderabad, and are seeking cooperation from Interpol to locate the accused.

articles.title: As police search for Khan sir, students gather in support outside Patna institute | India News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Faizal Khan, also known as Khan Sir, an educator and YouTuber, is being sought by police after he allegedly ordered his guards to open fire on a crowd outside his coaching institute in Patna.  Two days after the incident, Khan has not been arrested but videos surfaced online showing him defending his actions. Police increased security at key locations across the city while efforts continue to locate Khan. His lawyer claims the FIR was filed with a "retaliatory" intent and that Khan had no role in the alleged incident.

articles.title: Woman, Lover Accused Of Killing Her 5-Year-Old Daughter In Bengaluru
articles.rephrased_article: Priyanka, a woman from Bengaluru, and her alleged lover Mohan have been accused of murdering her five-year-old daughter, Vennila. The child died on March 24th, but the case was reported by the father, Praveen, nearly three months later.  Police arrested Mohan while Priyanka is currently at large.  The investigation is ongoing and awaits a report from the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL).

articles.title: ‘Not about Sikhism’: 11 Sikh MPs issue statement amid outrage over Henry Nowak's murder by Vickrum Digwa - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Eleven Sikh MPs, including Jas Athwal, Preet Kaur Gill, and Tan Dhesi, issued a joint statement distancing the Sikh faith from the murder of 18-year-old Henry Nowak. The MPs emphasized that the case was not about Sikhism, as the weapon used was an offensive blade, not a kirpan, and no religious exemption applied.  The MPs condemned the killing as a "horrific and senseless crime" and stressed that knife crime continues to devastate families and communities across Britain. They also called for an end to stigmatizing the entire faith community.

articles.title: Made In Pakistan Bedsheet Sold At Pune Religious Fair? Viral Video Sparks Probe
articles.rephrased_article: A woman in Pune, India, has accused vendors at a religious fair of selling Pakistani-made goods, including a bedsheet she purchased. The Centre banned imports from Pakistan following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. The police are investigating after the viral video sparked outrage and prompted the Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation to take action against vendors.

articles.title: Madhya Pradesh Man Attacks Teen's Face With Axe 20 Times, Tries To Hang Her, Arrested
articles.rephrased_article: In Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district, Dharmendra Parihar, an obsessed and jilted lover, brutally attacked a 17-year-old girl with an axe, injuring her severely. He then attempted to hang her from the roof of her house before she fell to the ground. The incident prompted villagers and the victim's family to block a major road demanding strict action against Parihar and his family.

articles.title: Turkish gang member convicted over plot to murder man outside family's London restaurant after £100,000 demand | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Beytullah Gunduz, 39, was found guilty of conspiracy to murder Onur Guzel, 38, who was shot outside his family's restaurant in Dalston, east London. The shooting occurred after Gunduz accused the victim's family of paying a rival gang £100,000 and demanded an equivalent payment. Prosecutors stated that the attack was linked to a long-running feud between the Hackney Turks (also known as the Bombacilar) and the Tottenham Turks.  The court heard that Gunduz orchestrated the shooting after the victim's family refused his demand. The case involved multiple incidents of violence against the victim's family and restaurant, including shootings and threats. Detective Inspector Iain Wallace from the Metropolitan Police condemned the attack as "calculated and ruthless" and said Gunduz showed a "complete disregard for the safety of both the victim and the wider community."

articles.title: Nagpur NEET aspirant's note not attached to case papers; show cause notice issued to Investigation Officer - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nikhil Tabhane, an Investigation Officer at the Ambazari police station in Nagpur, India, has been issued a show cause notice for failing to attach a note left behind by deceased NEET aspirant Akanksha Chaturvedi to her case papers. The note, written by Chaturvedi and discovered by her family days after her death, reportedly expressed concerns about scoring well on the retest ordered by the National Testing Agency (NTA) following allegations of a paper leak.  The incident has drawn national attention, with Rahul Gandhi, Congress leader, sharing it on social media.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Failure to attach a crucial note raises concerns about a potential cover-up.

articles.title: Punjab jalandhar Man 22 Killed In Raid. Family Alleges Encounter, Cops Claim Self-Defence
articles.rephrased_article: A 22-year-old man, Lovepreet Singh, was killed during a police raid in Bangiwal village, Jalandhar district.  Police claimed they fired in self-defense after being attacked by Singh's family who allegedly used sticks and stones. Singh sustained two bullet wounds to his waist and thigh and died at Nakodar Civil Hospital. The incident has sparked allegations of excessive force from Singh's family, who claim the police opened fire indiscriminately.

articles.title: Bar Owner Faces New Charge Over Swiss Ski Resort Fire That Killed 41
articles.rephrased_article: Jessica Moretti, co-owner of the Swiss bar Le Constellation, was charged with forgery over a falsified invoice for sound-insulation foam in the bar. The charge is related to the deadly fire that killed 41 people on New Year's Day and comes as Moretti faces multiple charges including manslaughter and arson by negligence. Prosecutors allege the foam ignited when champagne bottles with sparklers were raised into the air, while Moretti's lawyers claim the invoice was a legitimate purchase from 2015 unrelated to the tragedy.  The case has drawn criticism from victims' families who believe the Morettis are not taking responsibility for the disaster.

articles.title: Turkish gang member convicted over plot to murder man outside family's London restaurant after £100,000 demand | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Beytullah Gunduz, a member of the notorious Hackney Turks gang, was found guilty of conspiracy to murder Onur Guzel, who was shot outside his family's restaurant in Dalston. The shooting occurred after Gunduz accused Guzel's family of paying £100,000 to members of a rival gang, the Tottenham Turks.  Prosecutors argued that Gunduz orchestrated the attack after the family refused his demands. Dogan Over, identified as the gunman, fled the scene and is believed to have traveled to Istanbul. The Metropolitan Police Detective Inspector Iain Wallace called the attack "a calculated and ruthless attack" with a potential for loss of life.

articles.title: Cockroach Kingpin In Australia Caught With 1,00,000 Illegal Insects In Record Bust
articles.rephrased_article: Australia's Department of Climate Change, Energy, Environment and Water seized over 100,000 live Madagascar hissing cockroaches and dubia cockroaches in a single bust from a breeder in Bathurst, New South Wales. The seizure, worth $142,000, was the largest invertebrate bust in Australia's history and highlights the illegal import of exotic species despite strict biosecurity laws. Officials warned that these larger cockroaches could spread disease or harm native wildlife and urged pet owners to use legal alternatives for reptile food.

articles.title: NIA Arrests Ex-Trinamool MLA Saokat Molla In Bhangar Blast Case
articles.rephrased_article: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) arrested former Trinamool Congress MLA Saokat Molla, a prime suspect in the Bhangar bomb blast case, from West Bengal's South 24 Parganas district.  Molla was declared 'absconding' earlier this week after the agency conducted searches at his residence and other locations linked to him. The arrest brings the total number of individuals held in connection with the case to four. Molla will be produced before a court tomorrow, and further legal proceedings will follow.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Arrest of a politician by NIA raises concerns about potential abuse of power.

articles.title: Allahabad High Court grants bail to rape and murder accused over lack of scientific evidence - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court granted bail to an accused in a rape and murder case, citing insufficient scientific evidence linking him to the crime.  The court expressed concern over the lack of advanced equipment and staff at the Forensic Science Laboratories (FSL), stating that incomplete DNA profiles often prevent identification. The court directed the state government to improve FSL infrastructure and provide adequate resources.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Bail granted for rape and murder due to inadequate forensic evidence raises serious concerns.

articles.title: Supreme Court denies bail to Haryana travel blogger accused of spying for Pakistan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court dismissed the bail application of Haryana-based travel blogger Jyoti Malhotra, accused of sharing sensitive information with Pakistan. The court found no grounds for release due to the seriousness of the allegations and the nature of her activities, including alleged contact with Pakistani intelligence operatives.  Ms. Malhotra, who ran a YouTube channel called "Travel-with-Jo", is facing charges under the Official Secrets Act and Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The Haryana Police allege she was attempting to act as an asset for Pakistani intelligence, exchanging video footage of strategic installations with them.

articles.title: Three villagers killed, houses torched in Manipur; CM condemns attack - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Unidentified gunmen killed three Kuki villagers, including a woman, and torched seven houses in Manipur's Kangpokpi district early Friday morning. The Kuki Inpi Manipur (KIM) accused members of the National Socialist Council of Nagalim (NSCN) and its "proxy", the Kamson faction of the Zeliangrong United Front of carrying out the attack.  The KIM called for an investigation, justice, and security measures to protect vulnerable villages. The Kuki-Zo Council also condemned the attack, reaffirming their demand for a separate administration. Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the attack and promised swift action against those responsible.

articles.title: Lottery fund fraud: accused says he burnt currency notes - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sangeeth, a clerk accused of embezzling ₹14 crore from the Kerala Lottery Welfare Fund Board, confessed to burning ₹6 crore in currency notes after demonetisation. He allegedly withdrew the cash before the 2016 event and was unable to exchange or use it, prompting investigators to examine his residence for evidence. The alleged fraud spanned nearly a decade, with Sangeeth diverting funds into his own and associates' accounts.  The Vigilance department has attached properties believed to be owned by Sangeeth and seized a luxury car linked to his associate, Anil Kumar.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale embezzlement of public funds is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: Police book ‘Khan Sir’ in firing case; govt to curb coaching rivalry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Faisal Khan, known as "Khan Sir", was booked by the police in Patna on Friday, June 5, 2026, following an incident where his coaching institute, Khan Global Studies, was vandalized and a security guard attacked.  The attack involved multiple individuals from a rival coaching center, Gyan Bindu, who have been arrested. Mr. Khan has been named in an FIR and is expected to be questioned by the police. The incident has sparked controversy with political leaders blaming rivalry between coaching institute owners while some speculate that "trouble" may continue for Khan Sir.

articles.title: Over $580,000 forfeited in Australian visa fraud crackdown; man jailed for submitting false migration documents - The Times of India
articles.sentiment_target: man from the New South Wales Central Coast
articles.rephrased_article: Australian authorities seized over $580,000 in connection with a visa fraud scheme involving a 61-year-old man from the New South Wales Central Coast. The AFP-led Criminal Assets Confiscation Taskforce (CACT) took action to restrain and confiscate funds after financial investigations revealed the misuse of Australia's immigration system, including the Regional Sponsored Migration Scheme. The man admitted to providing false documents between 2017 and 2020, resulting in a court order for forfeiture totaling $583,146.44.  The confiscated funds will be used to support crime prevention programs, strengthen law enforcement capabilities, and fund community initiatives.

articles.title: Former Deputy AG booked over complaint against ex-Chief Secretary | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Saurabh Parashar, an Assistant Editor at The Indian Express, focuses on the socio-political landscape of Himachal Pradesh. He has over 17 years of experience in print media, specializing in crime, legal affairs, and investigative reporting.  His recent articles have explored issues such as drug trafficking, environmental concerns, and the impact of development projects on the state's unique geography. Parashar is known for his tenacious reporting on the state's drug epidemic and his ability to access remote regions like Spiti and Pangi.

articles.title: Allahabad High Court Grants Bail To Rape, Murder Accused Over Lack Of Evidence
articles.rephrased_article: The Allahabad High Court granted bail to Manoj, an accused in a rape and murder case, due to the lack of scientific evidence linking him to the crime. The court directed the UP chief secretary to address these issues and improve FSL capabilities.

The testimony adds to ongoing questions about the circumstances surrounding Epstein's death, which was officially ruled a suicide but has been subject to conspiracy theories for years.

articles.title: ‘Gurdwara is empty’: Sikhs scared to come out of houses in Southampton after Vickrum Digwa killed Henry Nowak - The Times of India

Community leaders have reported increased racial abuse, with incidents occurring at workplaces, public spaces, and even within gurdwaras. The situation has led to many Sikhs avoiding leaving their homes, fearing for their safety. This fear is fueled by the ongoing public discussion surrounding the murder case, which has been heavily criticized by community members who feel targeted and unfairly blamed for Digwa's actions.

Police suspect he died by suicide following the murder of his wife, which occurred early Wednesday morning in Thiruvananthapuram.  The attack reportedly took place in front of their daughter and followed a dispute between the couple that escalated into violence. Suresh had been on the run since allegedly slitting Haseena's throat. Police are continuing investigations into both the murder and death cases.

articles.title: Gurugram Man Strangles Wife To Death For Talking On Phone At Midnight: Cops
articles.rephrased_article: Narendra Singh, a 37-year-old laborer from Uttar Pradesh, has been arrested for the murder of his wife, Kajal Devi, 36, in Gurugram.  Police say Singh strangled Devi with a scarf after finding her on the phone at midnight and demanding her device. The incident occurred in their Bans Aliyar village home, where four children were asleep on the roof.  The police have recovered the murder weapon and are questioning Singh.

articles.title: Three men jailed over theft of 'priceless' golden helmet from Dutch museum
articles.rephrased_article: Three men were sentenced to nearly four years in prison for stealing a 2,500-year-old Romanian golden helmet from the Drents Museum in Assen. The heist involved an armed gang who broke into the museum and stole the helmet along with two gold bracelets.  The Dutch authorities recovered the helmet and two of the bracelets after striking a plea bargain with two suspects, while the third bracelet remains missing. Prosecutors had demanded a longer sentence for the third suspect, but the court imposed the same 47-month sentence on all three men despite the plea agreements. The theft prompted outrage in Romania and led to a dispute between the two governments over insurance compensation.

articles.title: Henry Nowak case: How handcuffed UK student's murder by Sikh man sparked national outrage - timeline of events - The Times of India

articles.title: Unocoin Bitcoin theft case: Karnataka Police SIT names Congress MLA N A Haris’s son in chargesheet | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mohammed Nalapad, a youth Congress leader, and his brother Omar Nalapad, along with hacker Sriki and his accountant Robin Khandelwal, are named in a chargesheet filed by the Karnataka Police for the theft of Bitcoin worth Rs 1.14 crore from the Unocoin crypto exchange in 2017. articles.title: ‘Doo Doo Water and a Few Needles’: Inside the Mystery of the New York City Manhole Prowlers | WIRED

The New York Police Department suspects these individuals are scavengers searching for valuables, but urban exploration content creators interviewed by WIRED say they don't recognize the men in the footage and believe it is unlikely that they belong to their community.  The creators emphasize that sewers are dangerous and rarely explored due to the lack of cell service and the presence of hazardous materials. The New York City Department of Environmental Protection has stated that there is no threat to public safety and that such activity is illegal.

articles.title: Khan Sir booked for attempted murder after ‘shooting orders’ — ‘Fire, I’ll handle what happens’

articles.title: Cops yet to solve Mumbai’s watermelon deaths mystery, no headway in fresh report | Mumbai News - The Indian Express

The police are awaiting a report on mobile phone data, but have not yet determined whether the deaths were suicide, accidental contamination, or murder. The family consumed watermelon and other food items before falling ill and dying within 12 hours.  Despite extensive investigation, including analysis of food samples and viscera, no clear explanation for the deaths has been found.

articles.title: Delhi Malviya Nagar hotel fire: Head constables who were the first respondents - The Hindu

Police officers rescued guests trapped inside after receiving a call from a caller reporting the fire. The investigation revealed that at least 18-19 rooms were occupied at the time of the incident.

articles.title: Delhi Mayor's Office Receives Bomb Threat, Declared Hoax
articles.rephrased_article: The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) received a bomb threat email on Thursday morning, prompting an evacuation and security response. Delhi Police and bomb disposal unit personnel were called to the scene, where the entire office complex was thoroughly searched for suspicious objects. No such items were found, and the area was sanitized.  Police are currently investigating the origin of the email.

articles.title: From Ritual Sacrifice to Labour Abuse: How Rajkot Police Unravelled A 2018 Mystery
articles.rephrased_article: The Rajkot police have solved a long-standing cold case involving the brutal murder of a child laborer.  In 2018, the severed head of the boy was found on the banks of the Aji River, initially leading investigators to suspect ritualistic human sacrifice. However, recent investigations revealed that Ajit Maula, alias Azmat Maula, a contractor from West Bengal, murdered the young migrant child after subjecting him to extreme abuse and dismembered the body to conceal his crime. The police are now coordinating DNA profiling to confirm the victim's identity and will seek charges against Maula and extradite him for prosecution.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Murder of a child laborer, potentially linked to exploitation, is a serious concern.

articles.title: Bengal Ex-Minister's Brother Arrested Over Extortion Charges In Kolkata
articles.rephrased_article: Swarup Biswas, brother of former West Bengal Sports Minister Aroop Biswas, was arrested by Kolkata Police on Thursday night in connection with allegations of extortion against technicians from the Bengali film industry. The arrest followed a complaint filed by a female make-up artist who alleged that Swarup Biswas had conspired to prevent her from receiving makeup assignments and extorted money from her through intimidation.  The case is being investigated at New Alipore Police Station, and Swarup Biswas will be produced before a lower court in Kolkata on Friday.

articles.title: Delhi University Professor Living Alone Found Murdered In Her Locked Flat
articles.rephrased_article: Devosmita Paul, an Assistant Professor at Shivaji College, was found dead in her locked flat in Vasundhara Enclave, East Delhi. Her sister, Devarati Paul, discovered the body after breaking down the door. Preliminary investigations indicate that she suffered head injuries and severed veins in her wrist, suggesting a homicide. The police have filed a murder case and are investigating the incident.

articles.title: Deputy Collector Arrested For Allegedly Raping Woman On False Marriage Promise
articles.rephrased_article: Arvind Mahor, a serving Deputy Collector in Madhya Pradesh, has been arrested on charges of rape and intimidation. The 32-year-old woman who filed the complaint alleges that Mahor exploited her sexually after promising marriage, culminating in a rape incident in Morena and subsequent repeated sexual exploitation at his official residence and Gwalior flat.  The case is under investigation by Civil Lines police, who are examining digital evidence including phone records, videos, and other communications.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a public official and alleged sexual assault are serious concerns.

articles.title: Dutch police investigate suspected drugging and sexual assault of multiple women
articles.rephrased_article: Dutch police are investigating suspected drugging and sexual assaults of multiple women, prompting the arrests of four men. The investigation was initiated after tip-offs from agencies in England and Germany, following information suggesting that victims may have been drugged by someone in their immediate circle and sexually assaulted on camera.  The suspects allegedly frequented private social media groups where tips were shared on how to drug victims and images of the abuse were circulated. The number of victims is not yet known, but more arrests are possible.

articles.title: Indian national Gurpinder Singh arrested for attempting to steal $495,000 in gold bars from elderly Florida woman - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A 20-year-old Indian national, Gurpinder Singh, was arrested in Florida after attempting to collect nearly $495,000 worth of gold from an elderly Gainesville woman. The scam began when the woman received a fraudulent email claiming her credit card had been compromised and instructed her to convert her money into gold.  Singh traveled from California to Florida to assist with the scheme, ultimately being arrested at a Chevron petrol station after attempting to collect the gold.

articles.title: Ahmed Al-Ahmed: Bondi attack hero Ahmed al-Ahmed charged with assaulting father: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ahmed al-Ahmed, a man who was widely praised for disarming an attacker during last year's Bondi Beach shooting, has been charged with assault in Sydney. Police received a report of an alleged assault at a home in Bankstown on March 9, 2026, and subsequently charged a 44-year-old man with common assault and stalking. The man is scheduled to appear before Bankstown Local Court on June 29. He has denied the allegations.

articles.title: 'Cocaine-fuelled' Brit jailed for life over murder of Saudi student Mohammed Algasim in Cambridge | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chas Corrigan, a 22-year-old UK man, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 22 years and six months for the murder of Mohammed Algasim, a Saudi Arabian student.  Corrigan admitted consuming alcohol and cocaine before the attack, which occurred outside Cambridge railway station in August 2025. The court heard that CCTV footage captured Corrigan approaching the group before stabbing Algasim in the neck. Algasim's father and sister gave emotional statements during the sentencing hearing. Peter Corrigan, Corrigan's father, was sentenced to two years for assisting an offender. Cambridgeshire Police Chief Inspector Dale Mepstead stated that the sentence reflected the seriousness of Corrigan's actions.

articles.title: Wipro Pune Ex-Staff Accuses Woman Boss Of Forced Religious Conversion
articles.rephrased_article: A former Wipro employee in Pune alleges she was subjected to religious harassment and forced resignation by her female boss from Bengaluru. The woman claims the pressure to convert to Islam, threats of poor reviews, and workplace intimidation led to her leaving the company.  The Pune Police are investigating the allegations, while Wipro states they are cooperating with authorities and have provided all relevant documents.

articles.title: Khan Sir's Coaching Guards Detained Over Alleged Firing During Vandalism
articles.rephrased_article: Bihar Police detained two security guards of Khan Global Studies Institute after a video surfaced showing them firing shots. The incident occurred following vandalism and stone-pelting at the institute by 15-20 unidentified individuals.  The police are investigating the matter, while a rival coaching centre director has been arrested for allegedly orchestrating the incident.  However, Khan Sir, founder of the institute, maintains that he was not involved in the firing.

articles.title: Uk Grooming Gang Survivor: ‘My childhood was taken away’: UK grooming gang survivor recalls abuse as 15 men jailed for 188 years - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Fifteen men have been sentenced to a combined 188 years in prison for the repeated sexual abuse of a teenage girl in Bradford. The men were convicted of 88 rape offences committed between 2007 and 2011, with some receiving sentences exceeding 13 years. Police praised the survivor's courage throughout the investigation and court proceedings, while authorities hope the case sends a message that child sexual exploitation offenses will be pursued regardless of time elapsed.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Large-scale sexual abuse of a minor is a serious crime and a failure of justice.

articles.title: Vickrum Digwa, father and brother appear in court over weapons charges day after murder sentence | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Vickrum Digwa, his father Moga Singh, and brother Gurpreet Digwa appeared in court on Tuesday following their charges of multiple weapons offences related to the fatal stabbing of 18-year-old Henry Nowak. The charges include possession of a flick knife, an extendable baton, knuckledusters, a machete, swords, and kusaris.  The case was adjourned until July 9th for further review of the charges by the Crown Prosecution Service. Gurpreet Digwa faces additional allegations including possessing an asp, a kirpan in public, carrying an axe in a public place, and possessing a prohibited air rifle.

articles.title: Woman’s body in a field, self-inflicted gunshot: How Kanpur Police cracked a murder case | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Kanpur Police have identified the body of a 21-year-old woman found in Bulandshahr,  Uttar Pradesh, after ten days. The victim had filed a complaint against a private hospital manager, Devkant Uttam, alleging sexual assault.  The investigation revealed that Uttam, his nephew Vivek Patel, and a security guard, Ajeet Singh, were arrested for the murder. Police believe Uttam strangled the woman after she refused to marry him. The victim's body was identified by her mother based on personal belongings found with the remains.

articles.title: Pune minor rape-murder case: Child witnesses among 32 examined before court | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A special court in Pune is hearing statements from 32 witnesses in the alleged rape and murder of a three-year-old girl. Special Public Prosecutor Ajay Misar said that evidence from seven medical officers was recorded on Thursday, and forensic experts will be called in on Friday. The accused, a 65-year-old man with a criminal record, allegedly lured the girl to a cowshed where he raped and murdered her. He is currently in Yerwada jail awaiting an "in-camera" trial.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Rape and murder of a child is a grave crime requiring urgent attention.

articles.title: 2020 Delhi riots: Court defers verdict in IB officer murder case for June 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi's Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh postponed the verdict in the murder case of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma until June 11th. The case involves Tahir Hussain, a former AAP councillor, and ten other accused who are charged with rioting, murder, and criminal conspiracy related to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots.  Mr. Kumar, Ankit Sharma's father, filed a complaint alleging that his son was murdered by the group at Hussain's office. The case stems from the communal violence that erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act in February 2020.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Delay in verdict for murder of IB officer during riots raises concerns about justice.

articles.title: Court halts Kerala policemen’s deal to drop charges after handcuffed body found in TN well | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Madras High Court has refused to quash criminal proceedings against seven Kerala Police personnel accused of illegally detaining a man during an anti-drug operation in Tamil Nadu. The court ruled that allegations of custodial misconduct and abuse of power cannot be settled through a compromise, as these cases involve serious questions about police accountability and the violation of constitutional rights.  The case stems from the 2017 death of Mokkaiyan, whose body was found in a well with handcuffs, leading to charges under the Indian Penal Code for offences related to custodial abuse and wrongful confinement. The court directed that the trial proceed expeditiously.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article reports potential police abuse of power and custodial misconduct.

articles.title: 2020 Delhi riots: Court defers verdict in IB officer murder case for June 11 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi court postponed the verdict in the murder case of Intelligence Bureau officer Ankit Sharma, who was killed during the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh deferred the judgment for June 11th, after hearing arguments from the prosecution and defense against 11 accused, including former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain.  The case stems from an FIR filed by Sharma's father, who alleged that his son was murdered by Hussain and others. The charges include rioting, murder, and criminal conspiracy.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Delay in justice for a murder during communal riots raises concerns.

articles.title: Bondi Beach shooting hero Ahmed al Ahmed charged with assault
articles.rephrased_article: Ahmed al Ahmed, the man who disarmed one of the alleged perpetrators in the Bondi Beach shooting, has been charged with domestic assault.  The 44-year-old was hailed as a hero after intervening in the December attack that killed 15 people and injured dozens. Al Ahmed denies the allegations of assault, stalking, and intimidation, which he claims are "not true at all." He is due to appear in court on June 29th. The Bondi Beach shooting was Australia's deadliest mass shooting since 1996.

articles.title: Why court refused to clear Madurai cop over Rs 1.45 crore counterfeit notes at abandoned quarters | Legal News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A Madurai district court refused to dismiss criminal charges against a police officer, Anand, who is accused of misappropriating seized property and engaging in extortion. The prosecution alleges that Anand, while serving as a sub-Inspector, failed to hand over all recovered counterfeit currency notes during an investigation into a 2021 case.  The court acknowledged inconsistencies between the initial FIR and witness statements but found that these discrepancies could be addressed during trial. The court also rejected Anand's arguments regarding a delay in registering the FIR and lack of sanction for prosecution, concluding that the evidence presented by the prosecution was sufficient to warrant a full trial.

articles.title: Henry Nowak Arrest: ‘So sorry’: Hampshire police chief apologises over Henry Nowak’s arrest after Indian-origin Sikh man misled officers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Constable Alexis Boon of Hampshire police apologized to the family of 18-year-old Henry Nowak, who died after being fatally stabbed by 23-year-old Vickrum Digwa in December.  The incident occurred after Digwa falsely accused Nowak of a racially aggravated assault. The bodycam footage showed Nowak repeatedly telling officers he had been stabbed and could not breathe while being handcuffed and arrested. The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) is investigating the handling of the situation. Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer, local MPs, and Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones condemned the violence that erupted following the release of the footage.

articles.title: Delhi Hotel Flourish Inn Fire Likely Caused By Short Circuit: Sources
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at the Flourish Stay hotel in Malviya Nagar, Delhi, tragically killed 21 people, including nine Indians and 12 foreigners. The blaze, which started around 8:30 am, spread quickly through the five-floor building due to a short circuit, according to preliminary investigations.  The fire department discovered more than four LPG cylinders in the hotel, along with electric stoves used for cooking by guests. Delhi Police are investigating the cause of the fire and the hotel's lack of a fire NOC and violation of bed and breakfast policy.

articles.title: CBI To Probe Death Of Ex-Kerala OfficialNaveen Babu, Daughter To Get Government Job
articles.rephrased_article: The Kerala government has decided to hand over the investigation into the death of former Kannur Additional District Magistrate Naveen Babu to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). The decision follows family demands for a central agency inquiry and concerns about unanswered questions surrounding his death, which occurred on August 15, 2024.  The government also decided to provide a compassionate appointment to Naveen Babu's daughter, Niranjana.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Family demands for a CBI probe due to unanswered questions about the death warrant concern.

articles.title: TMC councillor of Kolkata Municipal Corporation arrested for ‘molesting’ woman - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Biswajit Mondal, a Trinamool Congress (TMC) councillor of Kolkata Municipal Corporation Ward No. 114, was arrested on June 4, 2026, for allegedly assaulting and molesting a woman in March 2024. The arrest follows a complaint filed by the woman at Regent Park police station, who also alleged verbal abuse and threats from Mondal after the change of government in West Bengal last month. This incident comes amidst a wave of arrests targeting TMC leaders and elected representatives across the state for various allegations including extortion, intimidation, and corruption.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a public official is a serious concern.

articles.title: Indonesia arrests officials in crackdown on corruption | Corruption News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Indonesia’s deputy minister for immigration affairs, Silmy Karim, has been arrested following an investigation into alleged corruption in the administration of immigration documents. Budi Prasetyo, spokesperson for the anticorruption agency KPK, confirmed the arrest and stated that Karim was questioned for about 10 hours before being transferred to detention. The KPK has also identified seven other suspects in the case, which is believed to have occurred from 2023 to 2024 while Karim served as director general for immigration affairs under former President Joko Widodo.

articles.title: Failing to get remarried, Pune villager kills father and brother | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Babaji Jayram Mukne, 32, has been arrested for the murders of his father, Jayram Mahadu Mukne, 65, and younger brother, Rajendra Jayram Mukne, 30. The incident occurred near their tin shed house in Bagadwadi village on Tuesday night after a dispute over his marriage.  Yuvraj Mukne, 27, filed an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Section 103 (1) and police are seeking custody of Babaji Jayram Mukne for further investigation.

articles.title: UP Man Kills Family Over Property, Gets Killed By Friend Who Helped In Crime
articles.rephrased_article: Police in South Malaka, India, are investigating the deaths of three family members. Virendra Vaishya, his wife Anita, and daughter Meenakshi were found dead at their home on Tuesday. Their son, Abhishek Vaishya, was also found murdered in a shop on the ground floor. Police arrested Sunny Gupta, Abhishek's friend, who allegedly killed the family members and then killed Abhishek during a dispute over the division of valuables.  Gupta is currently under arrest and police are continuing their investigation.

articles.title: Exclusive | Licence in accountant’s name: How South Delhi hotel owner bypassed rules | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police are investigating the owner of Flourish Stays B&B, where a fire killed 21 people, after discovering he obtained the facility's license in his accountant's name. The building was purchased six years ago by Lavkesh Bajaj, who converted it into a B&B establishment despite not owning it legally.  Bajaj allegedly misrepresented ownership and expanded the property beyond its permitted capacity, potentially violating regulations. He is expected to be produced before a court on Thursday.

articles.title: Delhi Hotel Owner Lavkesh Bajaj Witnessed Fire That Killed 21, Fled Out Of Fear: Sources, Flourish Stay B&B, Hauz Rani, Malviya Nagar Fire, Delhi Hotel Fire
articles.rephrased_article: Lavkesh Bajaj, owner of the Flourish Stay bed-and-breakfast in Delhi, was arrested after fleeing the scene of a fire that killed 21 people.  Bajaj confessed to driving past the burning building out of fear and did not attempt to help those trapped inside. The Delhi Police are investigating whether the B&B complied with safety regulations, including having only one entry and exit point and sealed windows. Jai Mishra, the hotel manager, is also being sought by authorities.  The fire broke out in the basement and spread quickly through the five-story building, trapping many guests who were asleep at the time.

articles.title: South Delhi hotel owner saw property up in flames, fled: Police | Delhi News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at the Flourish Stays B&B in South Delhi's Malviya Nagar claimed 21 lives, with authorities investigating potential safety violations and a short circuit as the cause. Lavkesh Bajaj, the building owner, was arrested for failing to ensure adequate safety measures. The structure, which housed a basement, ground floor, and upper floors, lacked proper fire-safety arrangements and had multiple unauthorized construction alterations.  Police are also examining alleged food-safety violations at the restaurant operating on the premises.

articles.title: Babita Pandey: Uttarakhand MBA Student Missing During Dayara Bugyal Trek For 6 Days, 2 Friends Detained
articles.rephrased_article: A 24-year-old MBA student, Babita Pandey, went missing during a trek to Dayara Bugyal in Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi six days ago.  Her two friends, Harmanpal Singh and Harmanpreet Singh, were detained for questioning after her family filed a complaint. A 150-member search team is using drones, sniffer dogs, diving teams, and trekking routes to locate Pandey. The registration of the trekking agency, Pro Mountain, has been suspended as it was found that they used a fake permit.  The police are also investigating potential personal disputes or suspicious activity.

articles.title: Building Owner Arrested Over Delhi Hotel Fire That Killed 21
articles.rephrased_article: Delhi Police arrested Lavkesh Bajaj, owner of the hotel building where a devastating fire killed 21 people, hours after the blaze. The fire occurred at the Flourish Stay B&B in south Delhi and investigators believe the hotel was operating without a fire NOC and had numerous safety violations. At least 58 people were rescued and taken to hospitals, where 21 were declared dead. Police are examining the role of other individuals associated with the establishment and have registered an FIR under culpable homicide and other relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.title: New details surface as ChudTheBuilder’s release bid stalls despite Alex Rosen offering $100,000 toward bond - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, remains in jail after a Tennessee judge refused to lower his $1 million bond.  Eatherly faces serious charges related to a shooting outside the Montgomery County Courthouse on May 13, including attempted murder and aggravated assault. Despite arguments from Eatherly's attorney and father, Judge William Goodman III maintained the bond amount. Alex Rosen, YouTuber known for his Predators Poachers platform, offered $100,000 toward Eatherly’s release but was unsuccessful in persuading the judge to change the restrictions.  Eatherly also faces separate charges of theft and disorderly conduct stemming from an incident at a Nashville restaurant.

articles.title: New details surface as ChudTheBuilder’s release bid stalls despite Alex Rosen offering $100,000 toward bond - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Dalton Eatherly, known online as ChudTheBuilder, remains in jail after a Tennessee judge refused to lower his $1 million bond for charges related to a shooting outside the Montgomery County Courthouse on May 13. Alex Rosen, YouTuber and creator of the Predators Poachers platform, offered to contribute $100,000 toward Eatherly's release, but the judge maintained existing restrictions.  Judge William Goodman III also questioned a proposed arrangement involving LA Bonding and a surety company, citing concerns about money transfer capacity. Despite his attorney's arguments for reduced bond due to strong community ties and lack of prior convictions, Eatherly faces serious charges including attempted murder and aggravated assault.

articles.title: Petroleum dealers threaten to go on strike if action is not taken on those who damaged Thoothukudi fuel outlet - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Petroleum dealers in Tamil Nadu have threatened to strike if their demands for increased security and action against attackers are not met. K.P. Murali, president of the Tamil Nadu Petroleum Dealers’ Association, stated that they want the Goondas Act invoked against perpetrators, a crackdown on drugs, and protection measures for employees. The dealers are demanding safety assurances after an attack on an Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. pump in Thoothukudi left one employee injured.  The incident highlights the challenges faced by retail outlets, including security concerns and unruly customer behavior.

articles.title: Indian national Tarsem Singh charged in crash that killed pregnant teen, victim’s mother calls for ICE deportation: 'They can send him wherever' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ashlee Holmes, a 17-year-old pregnant teenager, died in a car crash in Ohio after being ejected from a vehicle driven by Tarsem Singh, an Indian national who faces multiple felony charges.  Singh was driving illegally and led police on a high-speed chase before losing control of his Range Rover, causing the fatal crash. Annette Holmes, Ashlee's mother, has demanded that Singh be deported, stating she does not want him in the United States. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed Singh entered the country illegally in 2017 and is currently being held on a $1 million bond.  Singh's trial is scheduled for August.

articles.title: Info panel rejects claim that CCTV footage in police station got auto-deleted - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu Information Commission has rejected the claim that CCTV footage from a Tiruvallur police station was auto-deleted. The commission criticized the Tiruvallur Town police for failing to provide requested footage and directed a supervisory officer to investigate the Public Information Officer's actions, potentially leading to disciplinary action.  The case stemmed from a petitioner alleging his mobile phone was taken and data erased by police without consent.

articles.title: UK minister condemns violent protests against student’s murder | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Shabana Mahmood, British Home Secretary, condemned violent protests in Southampton following the death of 18-year-old student Henry Nowak, who was handcuffed by police while dying from stab wounds inflicted by his killer. The riots, sparked by claims of "two-tier justice" that disadvantages white people, saw hundreds of protesters pelting officers with objects and injuring eleven. Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), and Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, a British far-right activist known as Tommy Robinson, have also expressed outrage over the case.  The Independent Office for Police Conduct is reviewing the actions of officers involved in Nowak's death, while the National Police Chiefs’ Council will review its antiracism guidance.

articles.title: Sex determination racket: 12th passout used portable sonography machine,15 doctors under scanner for female foeticide | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: A Pune Rural police investigation has uncovered a shocking sex determination racket in which a Class 12 dropout, Annasahabe Giri, allegedly used a portable sonography machine to perform illegal procedures on pregnant women.  He referred patients to doctors for female foeticide and charged over Rs 50,000 per case. Dr Atul Jadhav and Dr Sundaram Kadam, along with Dr Mandar Mali, have been arrested in connection with the racket. The probe has revealed that Giri performed an average of 30 to 50 sex determinations monthly and is suspected to be linked to at least 15 other doctors who are now under scrutiny.  The investigation is ongoing, focusing on establishing links between middlemen, Giri, and those involved in female foeticide.

articles.title: ‘Assault’ on women: lookout notice to be issued against main accused - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police are issuing a lookout circular for Ali Akbar, the prime suspect in an alleged assault on two young women at Kaloor, who has a criminal history and was previously booked in a POCSO case.  Akbar is accused of running an illegal prostitution racket under the guise of a lodging business. The three arrested employees, Alvin, Arun, and Sabith, are in judicial custody while Akbar and six others remain on the run. An identification parade will be conducted once all suspects are apprehended.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged assault, prostitution racket, and prior POCSO case raise serious concerns.

articles.title: Indian national Tarsem Singh charged in crash that killed pregnant teen, victim’s mother calls for ICE deportation: 'They can send him wherever' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ashlee Holmes, a 17-year-old pregnant teenager, died in a car crash in Ohio after being ejected from a vehicle driven by Tarsem Singh, an Indian national charged with multiple felony counts including involuntary manslaughter.  Annette Holmes, Ashlee's mother, has stated her desire for Singh to be deported as she believes he should not remain in the US. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed that Singh entered the country illegally in 2017 and is currently awaiting trial for his role in the fatal crash.

articles.title: 36 arrests in a day as Kochi City police launch ‘Operation Toofan’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi City police conducted a series of raids as part of the "Operation Toofan: The Narco Hunt" initiative, resulting in 33 NDPS Act cases and 36 arrests across 90 locations.  The largest seizure involved 437.28 grams of suspected MDMA found at Kollamkudi Mugal near Thrikkakara. Assistant Commissioner of Police (Narcotics Cell) T.D. Sunilkumar led the District Anti-Narcotics Special Action Force, which also includes teams from various police stations.  The operation was launched by Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and overseen by Inspector General (Intelligence) Putta Vimaladitya, who serves as the State nodal officer for the project.

articles.title: Application by driver’s mother in Porsche crash: Prosecution opposes plea for blood reports of victims, calls it ‘roving and fishing inquiry | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Aneesh Awadhiya and Ashwini Koshta, two young IT engineers, were killed in a Porsche crash in Pune. The prosecution has opposed the request of the mother of the accused driver for blood and viscera analysis reports of the victims, calling it a "roving and fishing inquiry."  The prosecution argued that at the stage of framing of charge, the accused is not entitled to seek documents the prosecution has not relied upon. Shishir Hiray, Special Public Prosecutor, submitted that permitting the accused to seek all unrelied documents at the pre-charge stage would amount to permitting a roving and fishing inquiry.

articles.title: CID arrests two in methanol supply chain in hooch tragedy, 20 deaths confirmed | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested a father-son duo, Arun Jagdamb Choubey and Abhishek Arun Choubey, who owned the company Rex International in Bhiwandi. The pair are suspected of supplying methanol to key accused Yogesh Ramchandra Vhankade, who allegedly mixed it with illicit liquor, leading to 20 deaths in Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad.  The arrests bring the total number of individuals in CID custody to eight. The investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Pseudo-police gang that kidnapped businessman and extorted ₹5.26 lakh busted in Cyberabad - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad police arrested five members of a pseudo-police gang who allegedly kidnapped a businessman, impersonated police officers, and extorted over ₹5 lakh from him. The suspects, identified as Nagaraju Raghu Varma, Yeswanth Singh alias Rahul, Sathyabhan Singh alias Thakur, Thangellapalli Nagendra Varma, and two others still at large, were apprehended following an investigation into the incident reported by a 42-year-old businessman in Kukatpally. The gang used fake police uniforms, forged identity cards, and other tactics to deceive their victims before withdrawing money from his bank accounts and assaulting him.  Police are continuing to investigate and identify additional victims.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Impersonating police and extorting money is a serious abuse of power.

articles.title: 2025 murder of gold merchant: HC asks DGP to take action against absconding BDO, orders action against investigation officer | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ordered the West Bengal Director General of Police to take action against absconding Block Development Officer Prashant Barman, who is accused in the murder of gold merchant Swapan Kamila.  The court also directed disciplinary proceedings against the investigating officer, Saswata Banerjee, for failing to uphold his duty. The court rejected the bail application of Trinamool leader Sajal Sarkar and ordered immediate action against Barman, who has been evading arrest despite a Supreme Court order.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Absconding accused and inaction by investigating officer raise serious concerns.

articles.title: TMC leader Jay Prakash Majumdar held over ‘grabbing’ woman’s house | Kolkata News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Jay Prakash Majumdar, a TMC leader, was arrested by the police in connection with allegedly illegally occupying a woman's house for several years and harassing her.  The arrest followed a protest against Majumdar outside his flat in Bidhannagar, where he allegedly assaulted some protesters. Meanwhile, Kolkata Police arrested Ward No 42 Councilor Mahesh Kumar Sharma on Wednesday in connection with a case filed in 2025.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Abuse of power by a TMC leader is reported as routine.

articles.title: How Pune IT firm duped nearly 700 techies before vanishing | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: ThynkTech India OPC Pvt Ltd, a tech start-up that recruited hundreds of engineering graduates across Maharashtra, abruptly shut down its Hinjewadi office in Pune. The company's CEO, Harshal Thakre, disappeared and failed to pay rent, maintenance charges, and electricity bills, leading to the sealing of the office.  ThynkTech India promised internships and job opportunities with a monthly stipend and a confirmed salary upon completion of training. However, interns were left without laptops, training, or compensation after discovering that the company was not legitimate. articles.title: UAPA Accused Madhesh Shankar Gets Bail After Nearly 5 Years In Custody
articles.rephrased_article: The Special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court at Patiala House granted bail to Madhesh Shanker, who spent 4 years and 9 months in custody for alleged terror activities.  Principal District and Sessions Judge (PDSJ) Pitambar Dutt imposed conditions including surrendering his passport, refraining from similar offenses, and not communicating with other ISIS members. The court noted the lengthy trial process and granted bail on a bond of Rs 1 lakh and two sureties of the same amount. Advocate Rahul Sahani argued for Madhesh Shanker's release based on prolonged custody and lack of apprehension to influence the investigation.

articles.title: 17-Year-Old Boy Stabbed To Death In Delhi, Probe On: Cops
articles.rephrased_article: A 17-year-old male was fatally stabbed in New Usmanpur, northeast Delhi. Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) Rahul Alwal stated that multiple teams are searching for the accused and a case under Section 103(1) of the BNS is being registered.  The incident has sparked fear among residents, with local police confirming the victim's identity as Abhishek, who lived nearby. The investigation is ongoing.
articles.civic_flag_reason: A young life lost to violence, highlighting potential law enforcement failures.

articles.title: Court allows CBI to arrest former Reliance ADAG executive Jhunjhunwala in bank fraud case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A Mumbai court allowed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to formally arrest Amitabh Jhunjhunwala, a former senior executive at the Anil Ambani-led Reliance Group, in connection with alleged bank loan misuse.  The court granted the CBI's request to formally arrest Mr. Jhunjhunwala, who was previously under judicial custody for money laundering charges. The CBI claims that Mr. Jhunjhunwala directed the misutilization of loan funds from banks, resulting in wrongful losses. The agency has filed a chargesheet against 16 individuals/entities, including Reliance Communications, alleging criminal conspiracy and misconduct.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Alleged bank fraud and misuse of power by a prominent business executive warrants concern.

articles.title: 'If it’s over, I’ll tear the house down': Drunk US man demolishes family home after wife says marriage is over - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Pennsylvania man, Eric Pierwsza, is facing charges after using an excavator to demolish part of his family home during a dispute with his wife. The incident occurred following an argument where Pierwsza threatened to tear down the house and was witnessed by his wife and two daughters.  Police arrested Pierwsza who faces charges including causing a catastrophe, reckless endangerment, and disorderly conduct.
